% The ring/repertoire boundary of section 5: what the ring buys, what it does
% NOT buy, and what blocks the way back. Three things a reader must not take
% away from this picture, and each was wrong in an earlier draft:
%
%   * splitting is a SIDE CONDITION, not a consequence. thm:relativised is a
%     biconditional whose right-hand side is "drop-safe AND A splits
%     proj(U)". So the middle of the chain is a yes/no DECISION with a live
%     "no" branch, never an arrow.
%   * completability is a HYPOTHESIS, not something the repertoire supplies.
%     A ring generated by a repertoire need not be completable in the
%     temporary's dimension. It is drawn as a premise entering the theorem
%     from outside the chain, never as a label on the ring node.
%   * the endpoint is a PROGRAM whose denotation is g (x) W. Writing
%     "witness g (x) W" names the tensor, not the object the theorem
%     produces; and U is the program being tested, so "g (x) U" is worse.
%
% Colour is not load-bearing. The premise and the decision are told apart by
% the word "assume" and by the question mark and yes/no edge labels, not by
% their amber rule; the blocked return is plum AND dashed AND struck through.
%
% WIDTH. \textwidth is 395.8pt; keep this under ~380pt or it overfulls.
%
%   make figures                                     compiles it
%   \includegraphics{figures/ring-repertoire}        includes it
\documentclass[tikz,border=3pt]{standalone}
\input{house}

\tikzset{
  % A hypothesis, or a question, that the chain does not answer for you.
  decide/.style={box, draw=accentwarm, line width=0.7pt, text=ink},
}

\begin{document}
\begin{tikzpicture}[house, node distance=8mm and 9mm]

  \node[box, text width=17mm, inner ysep=4.5pt] (rep)
    {a finite\\\textbf{repertoire}};

  \node[box, right=of rep, text width=19mm, inner ysep=4.5pt] (ring)
    {a \textbf{coefficient}\\\textbf{ring} $\mathcal A$};

  \node[decide, right=of ring, text width=23mm, inner ysep=4.5pt] (split)
    {does $\mathcal A$ \textbf{split}\\$\mathrm{proj}(U)$?\\[1pt]
     \footnotesize $=zz^{\dagger}$, $z$ over $\mathcal A$};

  \node[box, right=of split, text width=28mm, inner ysep=4.5pt] (wit)
    {a \textbf{separable}\\program, denotation\\$g \otimes W$};

  % the hypothesis the repertoire does NOT supply, entering from outside
  \node[decide, above=7mm of split, text width=34mm, inner ysep=4pt] (compl)
    {\emph{assume} $\mathcal A$ is $d$-completable};
  \draw[flow] (compl) -- (split);

  % the chain
  \draw[flow] (rep) -- (ring);
  \draw[flow] (ring) -- node[lbldim, above=0.7mm, font=\scriptsize] {$U$ safe} (split);
  \draw[flow] (split) -- node[lbldim, above=0.7mm, font=\scriptsize] {yes} (wit);

  % the refusal, dropping out of the decision
  \node[box, below=7mm of split, text width=34mm, inner ysep=4.5pt] (nowit)
    {$U$ is \textbf{not} weakenable\\over $\mathcal A$};
  \draw[flow] (split) -- node[lbldim, right, font=\scriptsize] {no} (nowit);

  % the way back, which is not free
  \coordinate (drop)  at ($(wit.south |- nowit.south)+(0,-6mm)$);
  \coordinate (backl) at (rep.south |- drop);
  \draw[->, draw=accentplum, dashed, line width=0.6pt]
    (wit.south) -- (drop) -- (backl) -- (rep.south);
  \node[fill=white, inner sep=2.5pt, text=accentplum, font=\large\bfseries]
    (blocked) at ($(drop)!0.5!(backl)$) {$\times$};
  \node[lbldim, font=\scriptsize, text=accentplum, anchor=north]
    at ($(blocked.south) + (0,-0.3mm)$)
    {back to words: exact synthesis, and not free};

\end{tikzpicture}
\end{document}
